questions.q: How often do you read most of this data?
questions.hint: Colder tiers save on storage and charge more to read it back.

options.label: Every day or every week
options.why: cool and cold charge $0.01 and $0.03 per GB read, so busy data is cheaper in hot

options.label: A little each month, well under half of it
options.why: in the post's arithmetic cool beats hot until you read about half of the data in a month

options.label: Almost never
options.why: cold storage is $0.0036 per GB and archive $0.001, against $0.021 for hot

questions.hint: Azure bills reads and writes in 4 MB steps.

options.label: Large, 100 MB or more
options.why: operations stay at cents and storage is about 99% of the bill in the post's examples

options.label: Small, under 4 MB
options.why: each small file pays for a full 4 MB operation, and premium operations are cheaper per call

questions.q: Do your tools rename or delete whole folders?
questions.hint: Spark and Hive often write to a temporary place and then rename it.

options.label: Yes, all the time
options.why: Microsoft says the hierarchical namespace makes a folder rename one metadata step

options.label: No, we only store and read files
options.why: hot writes list about 30% higher with the namespace on the page (East US against the East US 2 flat view), and Microsoft says some workloads gain nothing from it

questions.q: What matters most on the bill?

options.label: The lowest storage price per GB
options.why: hot is $0.021 per GB in East US against $0.023 for S3 Standard, and cool, cold and archive are lower still

options.label: The lowest price per operation
options.why: premium writes are $0.0228 per 10,000 against $0.065 in hot, and S3 requests are cheaper than hot ADLS

questions.q: Will you hold a steady amount of data for a year or more?

options.label: Yes, 100 TB or more
options.why: Azure lists reserved capacity for hot, cool and archive, but Microsoft says it is not available for premium

adls-hot.name: ADLS Gen2, hot tier
adls-hot.summary: Everyday storage with the hierarchical namespace. Hot is $0.021 per GB a month in East US.
adls-hot.bestWhen: You read the data often, your files are large and your tools work with folders.
adls-hot.watchOut: Hot writes list about 30% higher than the page's flat default view, and the namespace cannot be turned off once it is on.

adls-cooler.name: ADLS Gen2 with cool or cold tiers
adls-cooler.summary: The same account, with rarely read data moved to cheaper storage tiers.
adls-cooler.bestWhen: You read well under half of a dataset in a month and can leave it alone for 30 or 90 days.
adls-cooler.watchOut: Early deletion fees apply, retrieval is billed per GB, and archive can take up to 15 hours to read.

adls-premium.name: ADLS Gen2, premium tier
adls-premium.summary: Premium storage with the lowest operation prices, at $0.15 per GB a month.
adls-premium.bestWhen: You run a very large number of operations and care about low latency, the reason Microsoft gives for premium.
adls-premium.watchOut: In the post's arithmetic it takes about 3 million writes a month per 100 GB stored to repay the storage price, and reserved capacity is not available.

s3-standard.name: S3 Standard
s3-standard.summary: A plain AWS bucket. It has lower request prices and a hot storage rate of $0.023 per GB in US East.
s3-standard.bestWhen: You do not need real folders and care most about request prices, or your stack already runs on AWS.
s3-standard.watchOut: In the post's hot-tier examples the ADLS bills came out 7% to 8% lower, and we did not compare S3 colder classes.
